    AsyncHTTPClient ¶

    AsyncHTTPClient(
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
)

    Small retrying wrapper around :class:httpx.AsyncClient.

    Three transports are maintained:

    • a regular verified client used for TSETMC;
    • an insecure client used for every *.codal.ir domain, whose certificate chains frequently fail strict verification;
    • an insecure HTTP/1.1 fallback used once for TSETMC when the primary connection fails with an SSL/proxy-style error.

    Environment proxy variables are ignored by default (trust_env=False) to avoid corporate/VPN HTTP proxies breaking direct connections to domestic Iranian hosts. Pass proxy=... to opt into an explicit proxy.

    Create the pooled HTTP transports.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    timeout float

    Per-request timeout in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (30 s).

    		 DEFAULT_TIMEOUT
    max_concurrency int

    Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced by an internal :class:asyncio.Semaphore. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY (10).

    		 MAX_CONCURRENCY
    max_retries int

    Total attempts per request. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES (3).

    		 MAX_RETRIES
    retry_wait float

    Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT (0.5).

    		 RETRY_WAIT
    headers Mapping[str, str] | None

    Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal headers.

    		 None
    proxy str | None

    Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:9090". When omitted, environment proxy variables are ignored.

    		 None
    trust_env bool | None

    Whether to honour HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY and other environment settings. Defaults to True only when an explicit proxy is supplied, otherwise False.

    		 None

    Examples:

    >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
>>> client.trust_env
False
>>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
>>> client.trust_env
True

    def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Create the pooled HTTP transports.

    Args:
        timeout: Per-request timeout in seconds.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` (30 s).
        max_concurrency: Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced
            by an internal :class:`asyncio.Semaphore`.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY` (10).
        max_retries: Total attempts per request.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES` (3).
        retry_wait: Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in
            seconds.  Defaults to :data:`iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT` (0.5).
        headers: Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal
            headers.
        proxy: Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g.
            ``"http://127.0.0.1:9090"``.  When omitted, environment proxy
            variables are ignored.
        trust_env: Whether to honour ``HTTP_PROXY`` / ``HTTPS_PROXY`` and
            other environment settings.  Defaults to ``True`` only when an
            explicit ``proxy`` is supplied, otherwise ``False``.

    Examples:
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
        >>> client.trust_env
        False
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
        >>> client.trust_env
        True
    """
    self._semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)
    self._max_retries = max_retries
    self._retry_wait = retry_wait
    self._headers = dict(headers or {})
    self.proxy = proxy
    # Explicit proxies imply honouring the environment unless overridden.
    self.trust_env = (proxy is not None) if trust_env is None else trust_env

    common: dict[str, Any] = {
        "timeout": timeout,
        "follow_redirects": True,
        "trust_env": self.trust_env,
        "http2": False,
    }
    if proxy is not None:
        common["proxy"] = proxy

    self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        **common,
    )
    # Dedicated insecure transport for Codal (SSL chain bugs).
    self._codal_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**CODAL_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )
    # Last-resort HTTP/1.1 + no-verify transport for TSETMC.
    self._fallback_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )

    Perform a GET request with retries and TLS fallbacks.

    The request is retried up to max_retries times on network errors, and responses with status codes >= 500 are treated as retryable. A TSETMC connection that fails with SSLError/ConnectError is retried once over an insecure HTTP/1.1 transport. Every *.codal.ir request uses the dedicated certificate-relaxed transport.

    async def get(
    self,
    url: str,
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    raw: bool = False,
) -> httpx.Response:
    """Perform a GET request with retries and TLS fallbacks.

    The request is retried up to ``max_retries`` times on network errors,
    and responses with status codes >= 500 are treated as retryable.  A
    TSETMC connection that fails with ``SSLError``/``ConnectError`` is
    retried once over an insecure HTTP/1.1 transport.  Every ``*.codal.ir``
    request uses the dedicated certificate-relaxed transport.

    Args:
        url: Absolute request URL.
        params: Optional query parameters.  Ignored for URL encoding when
            ``raw`` is true.
        headers: Optional per-request headers merged over the defaults.
        raw: When true the URL string is sent verbatim without
            percent-encoding.  Required for the MarketWatch endpoint, whose
            ``paperTypes[0]=1`` brackets must stay literal.

    Returns:
        The successful :class:`httpx.Response`.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the host is unreachable, a non-2xx status is
            returned, or all retries are exhausted.

    Examples:
        >>> response = await client.get("https://cdn.tsetmc.com/api/BestLimits/1")
        >>> response.status_code
        200
    """

    target = self._build_url(url, params, raw=raw)

    try:
        async for attempt in self._retrying():
            with attempt:
                response = await self._send_with_fallback(target, headers)
                if response.status_code >= 500:
                    raise NetworkError(f"Server error {response.status_code} for {target}")
                response.raise_for_status()
                return response
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code} for {exc.request.url}") from exc
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"Request failed for {target}: {exc}") from exc

    raise NetworkError(f"Request failed after retries: {target}")

    async def get_json(
    self,
    url: str,
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    raw: bool = False,
) -> Any:
    """GET a URL and decode its JSON body.

    Args:
        url: Absolute request URL.
        params: Optional query parameters.
        headers: Optional per-request headers.
        raw: When true, send the URL untouched (see :meth:`get`).

    Returns:
        The decoded JSON value (usually a ``dict`` or ``list``).

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the request fails after retries.
        ParseError: If the response body is not valid JSON.

    Examples:
        >>> payload = await client.get_json(
        ...     "https://cdn.tsetmc.com/api/Instrument/GetInstrumentSearch/فولاد"
        ... )
        >>> "instrumentSearch" in payload
        True
    """

    response = await self.get(url, params=params, headers=headers, raw=raw)
    try:
        return response.json()
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ParseError(f"Invalid JSON from {response.request.url}") from exc

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
    """Close the primary, Codal and fallback HTTP transports.

    Safe to call more than once.  After closing, the instance must not be
    used again.

    Examples:
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient()
        >>> await client.aclose()
    """
    await self._client.aclose()
    await self._codal_client.aclose()
    await self._fallback_client.aclose()

    ParseError ¶

    Bases: IranQuantError

    Raised when a remote payload cannot be parsed into the expected shape.

    Covers invalid JSON, unexpected TSETMC/Codal schemas, malformed dEven or hEven values, and missing var datasource blocks.

    CodalLetter ¶

    Bases: CodalBaseModel

    CodalSearchResponse ¶

    Bases: CodalBaseModel

    A page of Codal search results with Pythonic container behavior.

    The wire-format field names (Total, Page, Letters) are kept for compatibility, and lowercase aliases (total, page, letters) are provided for idiomatic code. The object is also iterable, indexable and sized, and can be exported directly to a DataFrame.

    Examples:

    >>> response = iq.monthly_reports("فولاد")
>>> len(response) == response.total
True
>>> response[0].Symbol
'فولاد'
>>> response.to_dataframe()[["Symbol", "TracingNo"]].head()

    total property ¶

    total: int

    Total number of matching letters across all pages.

    page property ¶

    page: int

    One-based page number represented by this response.

    letters property ¶

    letters: list[CodalLetter]

    The letters on this page (alias of Letters).

    def to_dataframe(
    self,
    engine: Literal["pandas", "polars"] = "pandas",
) -> Any:
    """Export the letters to a Pandas or Polars DataFrame.

    Args:
        engine: ``"pandas"`` (default) or ``"polars"``.

    Returns:
        One row per letter with the declared :class:`CodalLetter` fields as
        columns (including nested extra fields is intentionally avoided so
        the schema stays stable).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``engine`` is unsupported.

    Examples:
        >>> frame = iq.monthly_reports("فولاد").to_dataframe()
        >>> frame[["Symbol", "TracingNo", "Title"]].head()
    """

    columns = list(CodalLetter.model_fields)
    records = [letter.model_dump(include=set(columns)) for letter in self.Letters]
    if engine == "pandas":
        import pandas as pd

        return pd.DataFrame(records, columns=columns)
    if engine == "polars":
        import polars as pl

        if not records:
            return pl.DataFrame({column: [] for column in columns})
        return pl.DataFrame(records)
    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported dataframe engine: {engine!r}")

    def resolve_codal_url(url: str) -> str:
    """Make a Codal link absolute (``/foo`` -> ``https://codal.ir/foo``).

    Protocol-relative links (``//cdn...``) become HTTPS, root-relative links
    are prefixed with :data:`iranquant.config.CODAL_BASE`, and absolute URLs
    are returned unchanged.  Empty strings stay empty.

    Args:
        url: A raw Codal URL as returned by the search API.

    Returns:
        An absolute URL suitable for :class:`httpx.AsyncClient`.

    Examples:
        >>> resolve_codal_url("/Report/123")
        'https://codal.ir/Report/123'
        >>> resolve_codal_url("//cdn.codal.ir/a.pdf")
        'https://cdn.codal.ir/a.pdf'
    """

    cleaned = url.strip()
    if not cleaned:
        return cleaned
    if cleaned.startswith("//"):
        return f"https:{cleaned}"
    if cleaned.startswith("/"):
        return f"{CODAL_BASE}{cleaned}"
    if cleaned.startswith("http://") or cleaned.startswith("https://"):
        return cleaned
    return f"{CODAL_BASE}/{cleaned.lstrip('/')}"

    def _resolve_letter_urls(letter: CodalLetter) -> CodalLetter:
    letter.Url = resolve_codal_url(letter.Url)
    if letter.ExcelUrl:
        letter.ExcelUrl = resolve_codal_url(letter.ExcelUrl)
    if letter.PdfUrl:
        letter.PdfUrl = resolve_codal_url(letter.PdfUrl)
    return letter

    async def _search(
    client: AsyncHTTPClient,
    *,
    symbol: str | None,
    letter_type: int,
    category: int,
    page: int,
    audited: bool,
    not_audited: bool,
    mains: bool,
    childs: bool,
) -> CodalSearchResponse:
    params: dict[str, Any] = {
        "Symbol": symbol or "",
        "LetterType": letter_type,
        "Category": category,
        "CompanyState": -1,
        "CompanyType": -1,
        "PageNumber": page,
        "Audited": str(audited).lower(),
        "NotAudited": str(not_audited).lower(),
        "Mains": str(mains).lower(),
        "Childs": str(childs).lower(),
        "Consolidatable": "true",
        "NotConsolidatable": "true",
        "Publisher": "false",
        "search": "true",
    }
    payload = await client.get_json(CODAL_SEARCH_URL, params=params)
    try:
        response = CodalSearchResponse.model_validate(payload)
    except Exception as exc:  # pydantic.ValidationError
        raise ParseError("Unexpected Codal search payload") from exc

    response.Letters = [_resolve_letter_urls(letter) for letter in response.Letters]
    return response

    async def search_codal(
    symbol: str | None = None,
    letter_type: int = -1,
    category: int = -1,
    page: int = 1,
    audited: bool = True,
    not_audited: bool = True,
    mains: bool = True,
    childs: bool = True,
    *,
    client: AsyncHTTPClient | None = None,
) -> CodalSearchResponse:
    """Search Codal announcements.

    Parameters mirror the ``search.codal.ir`` query API.  A temporary client is
    created and closed when ``client`` is not supplied.  Every returned letter
    has its ``Url``, ``ExcelUrl`` and ``PdfUrl`` resolved to absolute URLs.

    Args:
        symbol: Optional Persian ticker to filter by, e.g. ``"فولاد"``.
        letter_type: Codal ``LetterType`` filter.  ``-1`` means all types;
            ``58`` selects monthly activity reports and ``6`` selects interim
            financial statements.  Defaults to ``-1``.
        category: Codal ``Category`` filter; ``-1`` means all.  Defaults to
            ``-1``.
        page: One-based result page.  Defaults to ``1``.
        audited: Include audited reports.  Defaults to ``True``.
        not_audited: Include unaudited reports.  Defaults to ``True``.
        mains: Include parent-company reports.  Defaults to ``True``.
        childs: Include subsidiary reports.  Defaults to ``True``.
        client: Optional shared :class:`~iranquant.core.client.AsyncHTTPClient`.
            When omitted a temporary client is used and closed.

    Returns:
        A :class:`~iranquant.models.codal.CodalSearchResponse` with ``Total``,
        ``Page`` and a list of :class:`~iranquant.models.codal.CodalLetter`.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If ``search.codal.ir`` cannot be reached.
        ParseError: If the response is not valid JSON or does not match the
            expected schema.

    Examples:
        >>> response = await search_codal("فولاد", letter_type=58)
        >>> response.Total
        12
        >>> response.Letters[0].Url.startswith("https://codal.ir")
        True
    """

    if client is not None:
        return await _search(
            client,
            symbol=symbol,
            letter_type=letter_type,
            category=category,
            page=page,
            audited=audited,
            not_audited=not_audited,
            mains=mains,
            childs=childs,
        )

    http = AsyncHTTPClient()
    try:
        return await _search(
            http,
            symbol=symbol,
            letter_type=letter_type,
            category=category,
            page=page,
            audited=audited,
            not_audited=not_audited,
            mains=mains,
            childs=childs,
        )
    finally:
        await http.aclose()

    AsyncHTTPClient ¶

    AsyncHTTPClient(
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
)

    Small retrying wrapper around :class:httpx.AsyncClient.

    Three transports are maintained:

    • a regular verified client used for TSETMC;
    • an insecure client used for every *.codal.ir domain, whose certificate chains frequently fail strict verification;
    • an insecure HTTP/1.1 fallback used once for TSETMC when the primary connection fails with an SSL/proxy-style error.

    Environment proxy variables are ignored by default (trust_env=False) to avoid corporate/VPN HTTP proxies breaking direct connections to domestic Iranian hosts. Pass proxy=... to opt into an explicit proxy.

    Create the pooled HTTP transports.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    timeout float

    Per-request timeout in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (30 s).

    		 DEFAULT_TIMEOUT
    max_concurrency int

    Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced by an internal :class:asyncio.Semaphore. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY (10).

    		 MAX_CONCURRENCY
    max_retries int

    Total attempts per request. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES (3).

    		 MAX_RETRIES
    retry_wait float

    Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT (0.5).

    		 RETRY_WAIT
    headers Mapping[str, str] | None

    Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal headers.

    		 None
    proxy str | None

    Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:9090". When omitted, environment proxy variables are ignored.

    		 None
    trust_env bool | None

    Whether to honour HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY and other environment settings. Defaults to True only when an explicit proxy is supplied, otherwise False.

    		 None

    Examples:

    >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
>>> client.trust_env
False
>>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
>>> client.trust_env
True

    def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Create the pooled HTTP transports.

    Args:
        timeout: Per-request timeout in seconds.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` (30 s).
        max_concurrency: Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced
            by an internal :class:`asyncio.Semaphore`.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY` (10).
        max_retries: Total attempts per request.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES` (3).
        retry_wait: Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in
            seconds.  Defaults to :data:`iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT` (0.5).
        headers: Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal
            headers.
        proxy: Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g.
            ``"http://127.0.0.1:9090"``.  When omitted, environment proxy
            variables are ignored.
        trust_env: Whether to honour ``HTTP_PROXY`` / ``HTTPS_PROXY`` and
            other environment settings.  Defaults to ``True`` only when an
            explicit ``proxy`` is supplied, otherwise ``False``.

    Examples:
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
        >>> client.trust_env
        False
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
        >>> client.trust_env
        True
    """
    self._semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)
    self._max_retries = max_retries
    self._retry_wait = retry_wait
    self._headers = dict(headers or {})
    self.proxy = proxy
    # Explicit proxies imply honouring the environment unless overridden.
    self.trust_env = (proxy is not None) if trust_env is None else trust_env

    common: dict[str, Any] = {
        "timeout": timeout,
        "follow_redirects": True,
        "trust_env": self.trust_env,
        "http2": False,
    }
    if proxy is not None:
        common["proxy"] = proxy

    self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        **common,
    )
    # Dedicated insecure transport for Codal (SSL chain bugs).
    self._codal_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**CODAL_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )
    # Last-resort HTTP/1.1 + no-verify transport for TSETMC.
    self._fallback_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )

    async def get(
    self,
    url: str,
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    raw: bool = False,
) -> httpx.Response:
    """Perform a GET request with retries and TLS fallbacks.

    The request is retried up to ``max_retries`` times on network errors,
    and responses with status codes >= 500 are treated as retryable.  A
    TSETMC connection that fails with ``SSLError``/``ConnectError`` is
    retried once over an insecure HTTP/1.1 transport.  Every ``*.codal.ir``
    request uses the dedicated certificate-relaxed transport.

    Args:
        url: Absolute request URL.
        params: Optional query parameters.  Ignored for URL encoding when
            ``raw`` is true.
        headers: Optional per-request headers merged over the defaults.
        raw: When true the URL string is sent verbatim without
            percent-encoding.  Required for the MarketWatch endpoint, whose
            ``paperTypes[0]=1`` brackets must stay literal.

    Returns:
        The successful :class:`httpx.Response`.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the host is unreachable, a non-2xx status is
            returned, or all retries are exhausted.

    Examples:
        >>> response = await client.get("https://cdn.tsetmc.com/api/BestLimits/1")
        >>> response.status_code
        200
    """

    target = self._build_url(url, params, raw=raw)

    try:
        async for attempt in self._retrying():
            with attempt:
                response = await self._send_with_fallback(target, headers)
                if response.status_code >= 500:
                    raise NetworkError(f"Server error {response.status_code} for {target}")
                response.raise_for_status()
                return response
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code} for {exc.request.url}") from exc
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"Request failed for {target}: {exc}") from exc

    raise NetworkError(f"Request failed after retries: {target}")

    async def get_json(
    self,
    url: str,
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    raw: bool = False,
) -> Any:
    """GET a URL and decode its JSON body.

    Args:
        url: Absolute request URL.
        params: Optional query parameters.
        headers: Optional per-request headers.
        raw: When true, send the URL untouched (see :meth:`get`).

    Returns:
        The decoded JSON value (usually a ``dict`` or ``list``).

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the request fails after retries.
        ParseError: If the response body is not valid JSON.

    Examples:
        >>> payload = await client.get_json(
        ...     "https://cdn.tsetmc.com/api/Instrument/GetInstrumentSearch/فولاد"
        ... )
        >>> "instrumentSearch" in payload
        True
    """

    response = await self.get(url, params=params, headers=headers, raw=raw)
    try:
        return response.json()
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ParseError(f"Invalid JSON from {response.request.url}") from exc

    def resolve_codal_url(url: str) -> str:
    """Make a Codal link absolute (``/foo`` -> ``https://codal.ir/foo``).

    Protocol-relative links (``//cdn...``) become HTTPS, root-relative links
    are prefixed with :data:`iranquant.config.CODAL_BASE`, and absolute URLs
    are returned unchanged.  Empty strings stay empty.

    Args:
        url: A raw Codal URL as returned by the search API.

    Returns:
        An absolute URL suitable for :class:`httpx.AsyncClient`.

    Examples:
        >>> resolve_codal_url("/Report/123")
        'https://codal.ir/Report/123'
        >>> resolve_codal_url("//cdn.codal.ir/a.pdf")
        'https://cdn.codal.ir/a.pdf'
    """

    cleaned = url.strip()
    if not cleaned:
        return cleaned
    if cleaned.startswith("//"):
        return f"https:{cleaned}"
    if cleaned.startswith("/"):
        return f"{CODAL_BASE}{cleaned}"
    if cleaned.startswith("http://") or cleaned.startswith("https://"):
        return cleaned
    return f"{CODAL_BASE}/{cleaned.lstrip('/')}"

    def normalize_persian(text: str) -> str:
    """Normalize Persian/Arabic text for reliable comparison.

    Converts Arabic yeh/kaf/teh-marbuta to their Persian equivalents, converts
    Arabic-Indic and Persian digits to ASCII digits, removes zero-width and
    directional control characters, and collapses whitespace.

    This is what makes ``"فولاد"`` written with an Arabic yeh and the same
    symbol written with a Persian yeh resolve to the same TSETMC instrument.

    Args:
        text: Any string, including Persian, Arabic-Indic or mixed text.

    Returns:
        The normalized string with single spaces and ASCII digits.

    Examples:
        >>> normalize_persian("۱۲۳")
        '123'
        >>> normalize_persian("  علي  ")
        'علی'
    """

    translated = text.translate(_CHAR_MAP).translate(_ZERO_WIDTH)
    return " ".join(translated.split())

    def _extract_balanced_object(html: str) -> str | None:
    marker = _DATASOURCE_MARKER.search(html)
    if marker is None:
        return None
    start = html.find("{", marker.end())
    if start == -1:
        return None

    depth = 0
    in_string = False
    quote = ""
    escaped = False
    for index in range(start, len(html)):
        char = html[index]
        if in_string:
            if escaped:
                escaped = False
            elif char == "\\":
                escaped = True
            elif char == quote:
                in_string = False
            continue
        if char in ('"', "'"):
            in_string = True
            quote = char
        elif char == "{":
            depth += 1
        elif char == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return html[start : index + 1]
    return None

    def extract_datasource_json(html: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Extract the ``var datasource = {...}`` JSON object from a report page.

    A fast regex is tried first; if the JSON contains nested braces inside
    strings or is followed by more JavaScript, a brace-balanced scanner is used
    as a fallback.  Braces inside quoted strings are handled correctly.

    Args:
        html: The full HTML source of a Codal report page.

    Returns:
        The decoded datasource object, usually containing a ``"sheets"`` list.

    Raises:
        ParseError: If no ``var datasource`` block is found, the block is not
            valid JSON, or it decodes to something other than an object.

    Examples:
        >>> html = '<script>var datasource = {"sheets": []};</script>'
        >>> extract_datasource_json(html)
        {'sheets': []}
    """

    match = _DATASOURCE_PATTERN.search(html)
    raw = match.group(1) if match is not None else _extract_balanced_object(html)
    if raw is None:
        raise ParseError("No 'var datasource' object found in Codal report")

    try:
        parsed = json.loads(raw)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        raise ParseError("Malformed Codal datasource JSON") from exc
    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
        raise ParseError("Codal datasource is not a JSON object")
    return cast(dict[str, Any], parsed)

    def _parse_number(value: Any) -> float | None:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or value is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        return float(value)
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return None

    text = _special_to_ascii(value)
    if not text:
        return None

    negative = text.startswith("(") and text.endswith(")")
    if negative:
        text = text[1:-1].strip()

    sign = -1.0 if negative else 1.0
    if text.startswith("+") or text.startswith("-"):
        if text[0] == "-":
            sign *= -1.0
        text = text[1:].strip()

    if not _NUMBER_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):
        return None
    return sign * float(text)

    def _clean_value(value: Any) -> Any:
    if value is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        return float(value)
    if isinstance(value, str):
        normalized = normalize_persian(value).strip()
        if not normalized:
            return None
        parsed = _parse_number(normalized)
        return parsed if parsed is not None else normalized
    return value

    def _dedupe_columns(labels: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
    output: list[str] = []
    for index, label in enumerate(labels):
        base = label.strip() or f"column_{index + 1}"
        if base not in seen:
            seen[base] = 1
            output.append(base)
        else:
            seen[base] += 1
            output.append(f"{base}_{seen[base]}")
    return output

    def _normalize_column(column: list[Any]) -> list[Any]:

        return [None if value is None else _label(value) for value in column]
    return column

    def _row_looks_like_header(values: list[Any]) -> bool:

    return not any(_is_number(value) for value in non_empty)

    def _reconstruct_table(table: Any) -> tuple[list[str], list[list[Any]]]:
    raw_rows: dict[int, dict[int, Any]] = {}
    row_hints: dict[int, set[str]] = {}

    for cell in table.cells:
        if not cell.isVisible:
            continue
        row = int(cell.rowSequence or 0)
        column = int(cell.columnSequence or 0)
        raw_rows.setdefault(row, {})[column] = _clean_value(cell.value)
        for hint in (cell.rowType, cell.cellGroupName):
            if isinstance(hint, str):
                row_hints.setdefault(row, set()).add(normalize_persian(hint).lower())

    if not raw_rows:
        return [], []

    column_indexes = sorted({column for row in raw_rows.values() for column in row})
    if not column_indexes:
        return [], []

    ordered_rows: list[tuple[int, list[Any]]] = []
    for sequence in sorted(raw_rows):
        values = [raw_rows[sequence].get(column) for column in column_indexes]
        if all(value is None for value in values):
            continue
        ordered_rows.append((sequence, values))

    if not ordered_rows:
        return [], []

    header_positions: list[int] = []
    for position, (sequence, values) in enumerate(ordered_rows):
        hints = row_hints.get(sequence, set())
        hint_is_header = any(any(token in hint for token in _HEADER_HINTS) for hint in hints)
        if hint_is_header or (position == 0 and _row_looks_like_header(values)):
            header_positions.append(position)
        elif header_positions:
            # Only contiguous leading header rows are treated as headers.
            break

    header_rows = [ordered_rows[position][1] for position in header_positions]
    header_position_set = set(header_positions)
    if header_rows:
        labels: list[str] = []
        for column_index in range(len(column_indexes)):
            parts: list[str] = []
            for header_values in header_rows:
                label = _label(header_values[column_index])
                if label and (not parts or parts[-1] != label):
                    parts.append(label)
            labels.append(" - ".join(parts) if parts else f"column_{column_index + 1}")
        columns = _dedupe_columns(labels)
        data_rows = [
            values
            for position, (_, values) in enumerate(ordered_rows)
            if position not in header_position_set
        ]
    else:
        columns = _dedupe_columns([f"column_{index + 1}" for index in range(len(column_indexes))])
        data_rows = [values for _, values in ordered_rows]

    # Drop rows that became completely empty after cleaning.
    data_rows = [values for values in data_rows if any(value is not None for value in values)]
    if not data_rows:
        return columns, []

    normalized_columns = _normalize_all_columns(data_rows, len(columns))
    normalized_rows = [
        [normalized_columns[column][row] for column in range(len(columns))]
        for row in range(len(data_rows))
    ]
    return columns, normalized_rows

    def _build_frame(
    columns: list[str],
    rows: list[list[Any]],
    engine: Engine,
) -> Any:
    if engine == "polars":
        if not rows:
            return pl.DataFrame({column: [] for column in columns})
        return pl.DataFrame(
            {column: [row[index] for row in rows] for index, column in enumerate(columns)}
        )
    if engine == "pandas":
        return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=columns)
    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported dataframe engine: {engine!r}")

    datasource: dict[str, Any],

    """Reconstruct every visible table in a Codal ``datasource`` object.

    Cells are grouped by ``rowSequence``/``columnSequence``, invisible cells are
    dropped, header rows are detected (from ``rowType``/``cellGroupName`` hints
    or a text-only first row), and multi-row headers are joined with ``" - "``.
    Persian/Arabic digits, thousands separators, ``٫`` decimals, unicode minus

        DataFrame.  Persistently duplicated keys are suffixed with `` (2)``,
        `` (3)``, and so on.  Tables with no visible cells are omitted.  Values
        are numeric (``float``) when parseable, otherwise ``str``; missing
        cells are ``None``/``NaN``.

    Raises:
        ParseError: If the datasource does not match the expected structure.
        ValueError: If ``engine`` is unsupported.

    Examples:
        >>> datasource = extract_datasource_json(html)
        >>> tables = parse_codal_tables(datasource, engine="pandas")
        >>> next(iter(tables))
        'گزارش فعالیت ماهانه - تولید و فروش'
    """

    if engine not in ("pandas", "polars"):
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported dataframe engine: {engine!r}")

    try:
        model = CodalDatasource.model_validate(datasource)
    except Exception as exc:
        raise ParseError("Invalid Codal datasource structure") from exc

    output: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for sheet_index, sheet in enumerate(model.sheets):
        sheet_title = (
            normalize_persian(sheet.title_Fa or sheet.title_En or "") or f"sheet_{sheet_index + 1}"
        )
        for table_index, table in enumerate(sheet.tables):
            table_title = (
                normalize_persian(table.title_Fa or table.title_En or "")
                or f"table_{table_index + 1}"
            )
            columns, rows = _reconstruct_table(table)
            if not columns:
                continue
            key = f"{sheet_title} - {table_title}"
            if key in output:
                suffix = 2
                while f"{key} ({suffix})" in output:
                    suffix += 1
                key = f"{key} ({suffix})"
            output[key] = _build_frame(columns, rows, engine)
    return output

    async def _fetch_and_parse(
    client: AsyncHTTPClient,
    url: str,
    engine: Engine,
) -> dict[str, Any]:

    datasource = extract_datasource_json(response.text)
    return parse_codal_tables(datasource, engine=engine)

    async def fetch_and_parse_report(
    url_or_letter: str | CodalLetter,
    engine: Engine = "pandas",
    *,
    client: AsyncHTTPClient | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Download a Codal report page and parse all of its datasource tables.

    Relative URLs (including those on :class:`~iranquant.models.codal.CodalLetter`)
    are resolved with :func:`~iranquant.codal.search.resolve_codal_url` before
    the request is made.

    Args:
        url_or_letter: Either an absolute/relative report URL or a
            ``CodalLetter`` whose ``Url`` is used.
        engine: ``"pandas"`` (default) or ``"polars"``.
        client: Optional shared :class:`~iranquant.core.client.AsyncHTTPClient`.
            When omitted a temporary client is used and closed.

    Returns:
        The dictionary produced by :func:`parse_codal_tables`, keyed by
        ``"<sheet title> - <table title>"``.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the report page cannot be downloaded.
        ParseError: If the page has no valid ``var datasource`` JSON or the
            datasource structure is invalid.
        ValueError: If ``engine`` is unsupported.

    Examples:
        >>> letter = reports.Letters[0]
        >>> tables = await fetch_and_parse_report(letter)
        >>> for name, table in tables.items():
        ...     print(name, table.shape)
    """

    url = url_or_letter.Url if isinstance(url_or_letter, CodalLetter) else url_or_letter
    url = resolve_codal_url(url)

    if client is not None:
        return await _fetch_and_parse(client, url, engine)

    http = AsyncHTTPClient()
    try:
        return await _fetch_and_parse(http, url, engine)
    finally:
        await http.aclose()

    monthly ¶

    Monthly Codal sales analysis (LetterType=58).

    The analyzer understands the standard گزارش فعالیت ماهانه - تولید و فروش table: a product section followed by summary rows such as جمع فروش داخلی, جمع فروش صادراتی, جمع درآمد ارائه خدمات and a final جمع row. It returns the current-month, year-to-date and prior-year values in million Rials (the unit used by Codal) together with Month-over-Month and Year-over-Year growth percentages.

    AsyncHTTPClient ¶

    AsyncHTTPClient(
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
)

    Small retrying wrapper around :class:httpx.AsyncClient.

    Three transports are maintained:

    • a regular verified client used for TSETMC;
    • an insecure client used for every *.codal.ir domain, whose certificate chains frequently fail strict verification;
    • an insecure HTTP/1.1 fallback used once for TSETMC when the primary connection fails with an SSL/proxy-style error.

    Environment proxy variables are ignored by default (trust_env=False) to avoid corporate/VPN HTTP proxies breaking direct connections to domestic Iranian hosts. Pass proxy=... to opt into an explicit proxy.

    Create the pooled HTTP transports.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    timeout float

    Per-request timeout in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (30 s).

    		 DEFAULT_TIMEOUT
    max_concurrency int

    Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced by an internal :class:asyncio.Semaphore. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY (10).

    		 MAX_CONCURRENCY
    max_retries int

    Total attempts per request. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES (3).

    		 MAX_RETRIES
    retry_wait float

    Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in seconds. Defaults to :data:iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT (0.5).

    		 RETRY_WAIT
    headers Mapping[str, str] | None

    Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal headers.

    		 None
    proxy str | None

    Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:9090". When omitted, environment proxy variables are ignored.

    		 None
    trust_env bool | None

    Whether to honour HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY and other environment settings. Defaults to True only when an explicit proxy is supplied, otherwise False.

    		 None

    Examples:

    >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
>>> client.trust_env
False
>>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
>>> client.trust_env
True

    def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
    max_concurrency: int = MAX_CONCURRENCY,
    max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
    retry_wait: float = RETRY_WAIT,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    proxy: str | None = None,
    trust_env: bool | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Create the pooled HTTP transports.

    Args:
        timeout: Per-request timeout in seconds.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` (30 s).
        max_concurrency: Maximum number of simultaneous requests enforced
            by an internal :class:`asyncio.Semaphore`.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_CONCURRENCY` (10).
        max_retries: Total attempts per request.  Defaults to
            :data:`iranquant.config.MAX_RETRIES` (3).
        retry_wait: Base wait used by the exponential retry backoff, in
            seconds.  Defaults to :data:`iranquant.config.RETRY_WAIT` (0.5).
        headers: Extra headers merged over the built-in TSETMC/Codal
            headers.
        proxy: Optional explicit proxy URL, e.g.
            ``"http://127.0.0.1:9090"``.  When omitted, environment proxy
            variables are ignored.
        trust_env: Whether to honour ``HTTP_PROXY`` / ``HTTPS_PROXY`` and
            other environment settings.  Defaults to ``True`` only when an
            explicit ``proxy`` is supplied, otherwise ``False``.

    Examples:
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(timeout=10.0, max_concurrency=5)
        >>> client.trust_env
        False
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:9090")
        >>> client.trust_env
        True
    """
    self._semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)
    self._max_retries = max_retries
    self._retry_wait = retry_wait
    self._headers = dict(headers or {})
    self.proxy = proxy
    # Explicit proxies imply honouring the environment unless overridden.
    self.trust_env = (proxy is not None) if trust_env is None else trust_env

    common: dict[str, Any] = {
        "timeout": timeout,
        "follow_redirects": True,
        "trust_env": self.trust_env,
        "http2": False,
    }
    if proxy is not None:
        common["proxy"] = proxy

    self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        **common,
    )
    # Dedicated insecure transport for Codal (SSL chain bugs).
    self._codal_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**CODAL_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )
    # Last-resort HTTP/1.1 + no-verify transport for TSETMC.
    self._fallback_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        headers={**TSETMC_HEADERS, **self._headers},
        verify=False,
        **common,
    )

    async def get(
    self,
    url: str,
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    raw: bool = False,
) -> httpx.Response:
    """Perform a GET request with retries and TLS fallbacks.

    The request is retried up to ``max_retries`` times on network errors,
    and responses with status codes >= 500 are treated as retryable.  A
    TSETMC connection that fails with ``SSLError``/``ConnectError`` is
    retried once over an insecure HTTP/1.1 transport.  Every ``*.codal.ir``
    request uses the dedicated certificate-relaxed transport.

    Args:
        url: Absolute request URL.
        params: Optional query parameters.  Ignored for URL encoding when
            ``raw`` is true.
        headers: Optional per-request headers merged over the defaults.
        raw: When true the URL string is sent verbatim without
            percent-encoding.  Required for the MarketWatch endpoint, whose
            ``paperTypes[0]=1`` brackets must stay literal.

    Returns:
        The successful :class:`httpx.Response`.

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the host is unreachable, a non-2xx status is
            returned, or all retries are exhausted.

    Examples:
        >>> response = await client.get("https://cdn.tsetmc.com/api/BestLimits/1")
        >>> response.status_code
        200
    """

    target = self._build_url(url, params, raw=raw)

    try:
        async for attempt in self._retrying():
            with attempt:
                response = await self._send_with_fallback(target, headers)
                if response.status_code >= 500:
                    raise NetworkError(f"Server error {response.status_code} for {target}")
                response.raise_for_status()
                return response
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code} for {exc.request.url}") from exc
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        raise NetworkError(f"Request failed for {target}: {exc}") from exc

    raise NetworkError(f"Request failed after retries: {target}")

    async def get_json(
    self,
    url: str,
    *,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    raw: bool = False,
) -> Any:
    """GET a URL and decode its JSON body.

    Args:
        url: Absolute request URL.
        params: Optional query parameters.
        headers: Optional per-request headers.
        raw: When true, send the URL untouched (see :meth:`get`).

    Returns:
        The decoded JSON value (usually a ``dict`` or ``list``).

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the request fails after retries.
        ParseError: If the response body is not valid JSON.

    Examples:
        >>> payload = await client.get_json(
        ...     "https://cdn.tsetmc.com/api/Instrument/GetInstrumentSearch/فولاد"
        ... )
        >>> "instrumentSearch" in payload
        True
    """

    response = await self.get(url, params=params, headers=headers, raw=raw)
    try:
        return response.json()
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ParseError(f"Invalid JSON from {response.request.url}") from exc

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
    """Close the primary, Codal and fallback HTTP transports.

    Safe to call more than once.  After closing, the instance must not be
    used again.

    Examples:
        >>> client = AsyncHTTPClient()
        >>> await client.aclose()
    """
    await self._client.aclose()
    await self._codal_client.aclose()
    await self._fallback_client.aclose()

    Raises:
        NetworkError: If the report page cannot be downloaded.
        ParseError: If the page has no valid ``var datasource`` JSON or the
            datasource structure is invalid.
        ValueError: If ``engine`` is unsupported.

    Examples:
        >>> letter = reports.Letters[0]
        >>> tables = await fetch_and_parse_report(letter)
        >>> for name, table in tables.items():
        ...     print(name, table.shape)
    """

    url = url_or_letter.Url if isinstance(url_or_letter, CodalLetter) else url_or_letter
    url = resolve_codal_url(url)

    if client is not None:
        return await _fetch_and_parse(client, url, engine)

    http = AsyncHTTPClient()
    try:
        return await _fetch_and_parse(http, url, engine)
    finally:
        await http.aclose()

    def normalize_persian(text: str) -> str:
    """Normalize Persian/Arabic text for reliable comparison.

    Converts Arabic yeh/kaf/teh-marbuta to their Persian equivalents, converts
    Arabic-Indic and Persian digits to ASCII digits, removes zero-width and
    directional control characters, and collapses whitespace.

    This is what makes ``"فولاد"`` written with an Arabic yeh and the same
    symbol written with a Persian yeh resolve to the same TSETMC instrument.

    Args:
        text: Any string, including Persian, Arabic-Indic or mixed text.

    Returns:
        The normalized string with single spaces and ASCII digits.

    Examples:
        >>> normalize_persian("۱۲۳")
        '123'
        >>> normalize_persian("  علي  ")
        'علی'
    """

    translated = text.translate(_CHAR_MAP).translate(_ZERO_WIDTH)
    return " ".join(translated.split())

    def _to_number(value: Any) -> float | None:
    if _is_missing(value) or isinstance(value, bool):
        return None
    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        return float(value)
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return None

    text = (
        normalize_persian(value)
        .replace("٬", "")
        .replace(",", "")
        .replace("٫", ".")
        .replace("\u2212", "-")
        .strip()
    )
    if not text or text in {"-", "—", "_"}:
        return None

    negative = text.startswith("(") and text.endswith(")")
    if negative:
        text = text[1:-1].strip()
    sign = -1.0 if negative else 1.0
    if text.startswith("+") or text.startswith("-"):
        if text[0] == "-":
            sign *= -1.0
        text = text[1:].strip()
    try:
        return sign * float(text)
    except ValueError:
        return None

    def _numeric_cells(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> int:
    total = 0

        total += int(values.notna().sum())
    return total

    def _select_table(tables: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Pick the production & sales table, falling back to the most numeric one."""

    candidates: list[tuple[float, str, pd.DataFrame]] = []
    for key, raw_frame in tables.items():
        frame = _as_pandas(raw_frame)
        if frame.empty or frame.shape[1] == 0:
            continue
        name = normalize_persian(str(key))
        score = float(_numeric_cells(frame))
        if "تولید و فروش" in name:
            score += 1_000_000.0
        elif "فروش" in name:
            score += 1_000.0
        candidates.append((score, str(key), frame))

    if not candidates:
        raise ValueError("No usable Codal tables were supplied")

    candidates.sort(key=lambda item: item[0], reverse=True)
    best = candidates[0]
    return best[1], best[2]

    def _build_blocks(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> list[_Block]:
    starts: list[tuple[int, str, tuple[int, int, int] | None, bool, str]] = []
    for index, column in enumerate(frame.columns):
        label = _label(column)
        kind: str | None = None
        if any(hint in label for hint in _MONTH_HINTS) or ("دوره" in label and "ماه" in label):
            kind = "month"
        elif any(hint in label for hint in _YTD_HINTS):
            kind = "ytd"
        elif "اصلاحات" in label:
            kind = "adjustment"
        if kind is None:
            continue
        corrected = "اصلاح شده" in label or "اصلاح‌شده" in label
        starts.append((index, kind, _parse_date(label), corrected, label))

    blocks: list[_Block] = []
    for position, (start, kind, date, corrected, label) in enumerate(starts):
        end = starts[position + 1][0] if position + 1 < len(starts) else len(frame.columns)
        amount_index = end - 1
        for column_index in range(start, end):
            column_label = _label(frame.columns[column_index])
            if "مبلغ" in column_label:
                amount_index = column_index
                if "فروش" in column_label or "درآمد" in column_label:
                    break
        blocks.append(
            _Block(
                start=start,
                end=end,
                kind=kind,
                date=date,
                corrected=corrected,
                label=label,
                amount_index=amount_index,
            )
        )
    return blocks

    def _pick_period_blocks(
    blocks: list[_Block],
) -> tuple[_Block | None, _Block | None, _Block | None, _Block | None]:
    """Return ``(current_month, previous_month, current_ytd, previous_ytd)``."""

    month_blocks = [block for block in blocks if block.kind == "month"]
    ytd_blocks = [block for block in blocks if block.kind == "ytd"]

    current_month: _Block | None = None
    if month_blocks:
        current_month = max(
            month_blocks,
            key=lambda block: (block.date or (0, 0, 0), block.start),
        )

    previous_month: _Block | None = None
    previous_hint = next(
        (block for block in month_blocks if any(hint in block.label for hint in _PREV_MONTH_HINTS)),
        None,
    )
    if previous_hint is not None:
        previous_month = previous_hint
    elif current_month is not None and current_month.date is not None:
        earlier = [
            block
            for block in month_blocks
            if block.date is not None and block.date < current_month.date
        ]
        if earlier:
            previous_month = max(earlier, key=lambda block: block.date or (0, 0, 0))

    report_date = max(
        (block.date for block in blocks if block.date is not None),
        default=None,
    )

    current_ytd: _Block | None = None
    previous_ytd: _Block | None = None
    if report_date is not None:
        same_period = [block for block in ytd_blocks if block.date == report_date]
        if same_period:
            current_ytd = max(
                same_period,
                key=lambda block: (not block.corrected, block.start),
            )
        earlier_year = [
            block
            for block in ytd_blocks
            if block.date is not None and block.date[0] < report_date[0]
        ]
        if earlier_year:
            previous_ytd = max(
                earlier_year,
                key=lambda block: (block.date or (0, 0, 0), block.start),
            )
    else:
        usable = [block for block in ytd_blocks if not block.corrected] or ytd_blocks
        if usable:
            current_ytd = max(usable, key=lambda block: block.start)
        previous_ytd = next(
            (
                block
                for block in ytd_blocks
                if any(hint in block.label for hint in _PRIOR_YEAR_HINTS)
            ),
            None,
        )

    return current_month, previous_month, current_ytd, previous_ytd

    def _pick_total_row(labels: pd.Series) -> int | None:
    exact = labels[labels.isin(_TOTAL_LABELS)]
    if not exact.empty:
        index = int(str(exact.index[0]))
        return index

    candidates = [
        int(str(index))
        for index, label in labels.items()
        if any(token in label for token in _SUMMARY_TOKENS)
        and label not in _CATEGORY_LABELS
        and not any(hint in label for hint in _EXCLUDED_SUMMARY_HINTS)
    ]
    return candidates[-1] if candidates else None

    def _aggregate(
    frame: pd.DataFrame,
    total_row: int | None,
    category_rows: list[int],
    column: int,
) -> float | None:
    if total_row is not None:
        value = _row_value(frame, total_row, column)
        if value is not None:
            return value
    values = [
        value
        for value in (_row_value(frame, row, column) for row in category_rows)
        if value is not None
    ]
    return float(sum(values)) if values else None

    def analyze_monthly_sales(tables: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Summarize a monthly activity report's production & sales table.

    The main table is the one whose key contains ``"تولید و فروش"``; if no such
    key exists, the table with the most numeric cells is used.  Summary rows are
    detected by normalized ``جمع``/``مجموع`` labels.  A final ``جمع`` row is
    preferred; when it is absent, the ``جمع فروش داخلی``, ``جمع فروش صادراتی``
    and ``جمع درآمد ارائه خدمات`` rows are added together.

    Values are reported in **million Rials**, the unit printed in the source
    table.  ``prev_month_sales`` is only populated when the same table exposes a
    separate previous-month period; :func:`monthly_sales_summary` fills it by
    parsing the previous monthly letter.

    Args:
        tables: The mapping returned by
            :func:`~iranquant.codal.parser.fetch_and_parse_report` (or
            :func:`~iranquant.codal.parser.parse_codal_tables`), with Pandas or
            Polars DataFrames as values.

    Returns:
        A dictionary with:

        * ``table_key`` (``str``) — key of the selected table.
        * ``period_end`` (``str | None``) — latest reporting date in the table.
        * ``current_month_sales`` (``float | None``) — one-month sales amount.
        * ``prev_month_sales`` (``float | None``) — previous standalone month,
            when present in the same table.
        * ``ytd_sales`` (``float | None``) — year-to-date sales amount.
        * ``prev_ytd_sales`` (``float | None``) — prior-year YTD sales amount.
        * ``mom_change_pct`` (``float | None``) — month-over-month percentage.
        * ``yoy_change_pct`` (``float | None``) — year-over-year percentage.
        * ``summary_df`` (``pandas.DataFrame``) — filtered summary rows.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``tables`` is empty or contains no usable table.
        TypeError: If a table value is not a Pandas or Polars DataFrame.

    Examples:
        >>> letter = iq.monthly_reports("فولاد").Letters[0]
        >>> tables = iq.parse_codal_report(letter)
        >>> summary = iq.analyze_monthly_sales(tables)
        >>> summary["current_month_sales"]
        662639489.0
        >>> summary["summary_df"][["شرح - نام محصول"]]
    """

    table_key, frame = _select_table(tables)
    label_column = frame.columns[0]
    labels = frame[label_column].map(_label)

    summary_mask = labels.str.contains("جمع|مجموع", regex=True, na=False)
    summary_df = frame.loc[summary_mask].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

    total_row = _pick_total_row(labels)
    category_rows = [int(str(index)) for index in labels[labels.isin(_CATEGORY_LABELS)].index]

    blocks = _build_blocks(frame)
    current_month, previous_month, current_ytd, previous_ytd = _pick_period_blocks(blocks)

    current_month_sales = (
        _aggregate(frame, total_row, category_rows, current_month.amount_index)
        if current_month is not None
        else None
    )
    prev_month_sales = (
        _aggregate(frame, total_row, category_rows, previous_month.amount_index)
        if previous_month is not None
        else None
    )
    ytd_sales = (
        _aggregate(frame, total_row, category_rows, current_ytd.amount_index)
        if current_ytd is not None
        else None
    )
    prev_ytd_sales = (
        _aggregate(frame, total_row, category_rows, previous_ytd.amount_index)
        if previous_ytd is not None
        else None
    )

    period_end = None
    if current_month is not None and current_month.date is not None:
        period_end = "{:04d}-{:02d}-{:02d}".format(*current_month.date)
    elif current_ytd is not None and current_ytd.date is not None:
        period_end = "{:04d}-{:02d}-{:02d}".format(*current_ytd.date)

    return {
        "table_key": table_key,
        "period_end": period_end,
        "current_month_sales": current_month_sales,
        "prev_month_sales": prev_month_sales,
        "ytd_sales": ytd_sales,
        "prev_ytd_sales": prev_ytd_sales,
        "mom_change_pct": _pct_change(current_month_sales, prev_month_sales),
        "yoy_change_pct": _pct_change(ytd_sales, prev_ytd_sales),
        "summary_df": summary_df,
    }

    async def monthly_sales_summary(
    symbol: str,
    page: int = 1,
    *,
    client: AsyncHTTPClient | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Fetch and analyze a symbol's latest monthly sales report.

    The newest report on ``page`` is parsed, and its previous distinct monthly
    period is parsed too so a true Month-over-Month comparison can be computed.

    Args:
        symbol: Persian ticker, e.g. ``"فولاد"``.
        page: One-based Codal result page.  Defaults to ``1``.
        client: Optional shared :class:`~iranquant.core.client.AsyncHTTPClient`.

    Returns:
        The dictionary from :func:`analyze_monthly_sales` plus
        ``symbol``, ``tracing_no``, ``title``, ``prev_month_tracing_no`` and a
        ``mom_change_pct`` derived from the previous month's report.

    Raises:
        ParseError: If Codal returns no HTML monthly reports.
        NetworkError: If Codal or the report page cannot be fetched.
        ValueError: If the latest report has no usable tables.

    Examples:
        >>> summary = await monthly_sales_summary("فولاد")
        >>> summary["current_month_sales"]
        >>> summary["mom_change_pct"]
    """

    reports = await get_monthly_reports(symbol, page=page, client=client)
    letters = [letter for letter in reports.Letters if letter.HasHtml and letter.Url]
    if not letters:
        raise ParseError(f"No HTML monthly report found for {symbol!r}")

    def sort_key(letter: Any) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int], int]:
        period = _letter_period(letter) or (0, 0, 0)
        return period, int(getattr(letter, "TracingNo", 0) or 0)

    ordered = sorted(letters, key=sort_key, reverse=True)
    latest = ordered[0]
    latest_period = _letter_period(latest)

    tables = await fetch_and_parse_report(latest, client=client)
    result = analyze_monthly_sales(tables)
    result.update(
        {
            "symbol": normalize_persian(symbol),
            "tracing_no": latest.TracingNo,
            "title": latest.Title,
            "page": page,
        }
    )

    previous = next(
        (
            letter
            for letter in ordered[1:]
            if latest_period is None or (_letter_period(letter) or (0, 0, 0)) < latest_period
        ),
        None,
    )
    if previous is None:
        return result

    try:
        previous_tables = await fetch_and_parse_report(previous, client=client)
        previous_result = analyze_monthly_sales(previous_tables)
    except (IranQuantError, ValueError, TypeError):
        return result

    previous_sales = previous_result.get("current_month_sales")
    if isinstance(previous_sales, (int, float)):
        result["prev_month_sales"] = float(previous_sales)
        result["prev_month_tracing_no"] = previous.TracingNo
        current_sales = result.get("current_month_sales")
        result["mom_change_pct"] = _pct_change(
            float(current_sales) if isinstance(current_sales, (int, float)) else None,
            float(previous_sales),
        )
    return result
